summary: Cuilan Liu works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. She held posts as Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and at the University of Munich (attested 2018).

Culadasa (1944–2021) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied under traditional teacher Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu, taught Matthew Immergut, and served as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha (attested 2011).
Cuma Ozkan specializes in religious studies and sinology. He earned a Master of Arts at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).
Cunda studied under Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro.

Cuong T. Mai works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, completed a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington under John R. McRae, and became an Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.

Cynthea J. Bogel is a scholar of Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral studies under John M. Rosenfield and held a post at the University of Washington (attested 2004–2009).
Cynthia Col specializes in sinology and religious studies. She studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) and was taught by Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.

Cynthia M. Beall (born 1949) specializes in Tibetology. She completed a BA at the University of Pennsylvania and an MA at Pennsylvania State University before joining Case Western Reserve University in 1976 as Distinguished University Professor and S. Idell Pyle Professor of Anthropology.

Cynthia Talbot (born 1952) is an Indologist and historian. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and became Professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin, where she held a post from circa 1994.

Cyril Alexander Rylands was an Indologist and linguist who earned his BA and MA from the University of Cambridge. He served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London until 1961, teaching Thomas Welbourne Clark and Ludo Rocher.

Cyril Henry Philips (1912–2005) was a historian and Indologist. After studying at the University of Liverpool and earning a PhD from SOAS, he served as Director of SOAS (1946–1980) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of London (1972–1976).
Cyril Walter Gurner (1888–1960) was a scholar in Indology. He earned MAs from Oriel College (~1907–1911) and the University of London, and served as Treasurer of The Asiatic Society (attested 1944).

Cyrill von Korvin-Krasinski (1905–1992) was a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz by 1948 and served as director of the abbey’s school at Maria Laach Abbey.

Cyrus Ransom Pangborn (1916–1989) worked in religious studies and Indology, studying at Kansas Wesleyan, Yale, and Columbia. He taught religion at the University of Iowa (1951–1954) and was Associate Professor of Religion at Rutgers University (1954–1982).

Cyrus Stearns is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Leonard van der Kuijp, also studying under Turrell V. Wylie and several traditional teachers. He served as a translator at the Tsadra Foundation.
Cândido de Figueiredo (1846–1925) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied law at the University of Coimbra (1869–1874) and worked as a teacher at Liceu Central from 1882.
Cécile Ducher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Matthew T. Kapstein and served as a research fellow there.

Célestin Bouglé (1870–1940) was a philosopher and Indologist educated at the École Normale Supérieure. He held posts at the universities of Montpellier, Toulouse, and Paris (Sorbonne), and later served as Director of the École Normale Supérieure (1935–1940).

D. C. Lau (1921–2010) was a sinologist and philosopher educated at the University of Hong Kong and University of Glasgow. He held chairs at the University of London and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (1978–1989).
D. C. Sarasvati is an Indologist who studied under V. Raghavan. She served as Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras from 1964 to 1965.
